sentence_stem: When I was a child, I used to
correct_completion: play in the park every afternoon.
full_sentence: When I was a child, I used to play in the park every afternoon.
acceptable_variants: go to the park every afternoon.
spend every afternoon in the park.

options.text: I played in the park once last week.
options.why_wrong: This describes a single past event, not a repeated past habit, so 'used to' does not fit.

options.text: I am going to play in the park tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: This is a future plan, but 'used to' describes past habits.

options.text: play in the park every afternoon.
playing in the park since last year.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect continuous describes an activity that continues now, not a finished past habit.

grammar_focus: 'Used to' + base verb for past habits
explanation: 'Used to' is always followed by the base form of a verb and describes a habit or state that no longer happens. Polish speakers often use a simple past or a present tense here, because Polish has no separate form for past habits.
translation: Kiedy byłem dzieckiem, zwykłem bawić się w parku każdego popołudnia.
